title: PII deletion witness service and backfill safety-net
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a standalone 'deletion witness' service and a backfill safety-net for console analytics pipelines to ensure PII removal completes and can be cryptographically attested. The witness service will receive canonical deletion intents (from API-level erase requests, retention governance jobs, and legal holds), track their lifecycle through the analytics pipeline, and emit an auditable attestation when deletion has been materialized in downstream stores (clickstream shards, OLAP snapshots, ephemeral views, and derived metrics). The backfill safety-net coordinates when the primary streaming deletion path falls behind (consumer lag, schema drift, node failures) and runs targeted removal jobs against persisted stores with strong idempotency and cost controls. The feature must provide: 1) provable retention enforcement (deletion attestations that can be exported to customers/legal), 2) bounded operational cost for backfills, 3) clear observability and runbooks for SRE/Support, and 4) minimal change surface on upstream producers. This ticket scopes the core service API, state model, one streaming connector (Kafka -> witness), one backfill worker for BigQuery/OLAP, observability dashboards, and runbook + legal attestation export format. Out of scope: multi-tenant data rekeying, HSM-managed proofs, and UI work in Console (will be a follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Witness service accepts canonical deletion intents from API and ingestion jobs and returns a canonical ID within 1s
Attestation record (JSON-LD) is written to internal audit topic within 30s of materialization in downstream store for >95% of low-latency cases
Backfill worker can run idempotent deletions against a snapshoted OLAP table with a safety throttle and complete a 1M-row targeted backfill without exceeding cost budget in staging
End-to-end test harness (local + CI) simulates consumer lag and validates backfill triggers and attestations
Runbook created and on-call SRE accepted the escalation path and rollback steps
Legal/Compliance reviewed and approved attestation export format
architecture_decisions: Use an append-only witness store (immutable attestations) instead of destructive tombstones to preserve auditability and simplify replay
Emit attestations to an internal Kafka topic (privacy-audit) for durability and to allow downstream exports; do not expose raw attestations to customers directly — use an export job
Backfill will be pull-based and orchestrated by the witness coordinator rather than pushing deletion SQL to all services — reduces blast radius and centralizes retry/rollback
Use cryptographic signing of attestations with service keys (rotated via KMS) rather than full HSM at MVP; HSM integration deferred
Favor eventual consistency for analytics stores; provide SLA of materialization time windows and include that in attestation metadata
Keep witness lightweight: store opaque deletion tokens + origin metadata; do not replicate full PII payloads into the witness store
implementation_plan: API surface: POST /deletions (idempotent) and GET /deletions/{id}/attestations — 3 days
Kafka consumer connector for ingestion pipeline to publish deletion intents into witness topic — 4 days
Backfill worker for OLAP (BigQuery prototype) with safety throttles and dry-run mode — 6 days
Observability: Prometheus metrics (attestations/sec, lag, backfill jobs running), Grafana dashboard — 3 days
Export job to produce customer-facing attestation bundles and signed manifests — 2 days
End-to-end tests and CI harness (local emulation of streaming + backfill) — 4 days
Runbook + SRE onboarding + legal sign-off — 3 days
Canary rollout in staging then production with feature-flag gating — 2 days
testing_plan: Unit tests for API idempotency and signature validation
Integration tests: publish deletion intent, simulate consumer lag, assert backfill trigger and attestation emission
Load test the witness topic at expected peak ingestion (10k deletion intents/min) and validate ELs and retention costs
Chaos: kill connector worker during deletion, ensure safe retries and no double-purge
Security review: threat model and penetration checklist for export job
Compliance scenario tests: export attestation bundle for a simulated DSAR and validate signatures and timestamps
rollouts: Feature flag gate: initial rollout only for internal org 'redwood-internal'
Staging: run full streaming + backfill against staging analytics data for 72h
Gradual region rollout: us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1; monitor lag and backfill volume
Full tenant opt-in after legal attestation export sign-off and SRE on-call readiness
